chapter: Touring shows and the bands he heard
title: How devoted audiences were to the bands
summary: People saved for weeks to dress for a dance, and many stood listening because radio and records were all there was; he compares Europe.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: Well, I heard all these people, you know. I used to listen to them on the records, you know. It was a really, really nice time, because people were really into the music. Like, people would save up money for weeks to get ready for the dance. They'd be saving for weeks when the bands would come down to play the dance, and they'd be ready, you know, with new outfits and new hairdos and everything. They'd really get ready when the band came to town. Maybe...maybe ... At least 25 percent of them would be standing around listening to the music, and the other people could be

dancing, but they'd be standing around listening to the music -- because people were into music. Because radio was all we had. Radio and records. There was no television, you know. It's pretty much like Europe is now. See, radio is real big in Europe because there's not too many television sets over there. Radio is big in Europe...

Yeah, well, that's why! That's what it is. Like, today in most of the major cities in Europe, you don't actually get television shows until around about five in the evening -- five o'clock. And the rest, you get records played on the television!
